_schema._comment: Collector join specifications. One profile per collector, giving the fields a record format exposes and how records join into provenance operations. A profile is per PRODUCT of the collector, never per CVE: it encodes what a log format records, not what any exploit looks like. Reused unchanged across every CVE.

_fields.format: the on-disk record format the collector emits
_fields.selects: record selector: the field/value test admitting a record to this profile
_fields.subject: field naming the process the collector attributes the operation to
_fields.object: field naming the entity operated on
_fields.peer: field naming the remote endpoint of an exchange, when the record has one
_fields.class: how the record's event class in Sigma_sigma is derived
_fields.join: how separate records correlate into one operation, when the format splits them
_fields.normalization: the URL/path normalization profile this collector's labels compare under

sysmon-process.format: Windows Sysmon XML/EVTX, rendered as key=value by the forwarder
sysmon-process.subject: Image
sysmon-process.object: TargetFilename for file events, TargetObject for registry events, Image for process creation
sysmon-process.class: EventID 1 -> create; 11 -> write; 23 -> write; 12/13 -> write (registry); 5 -> close
sysmon-process.join: ProcessGuid links a child record to its parent through ParentProcessGuid, giving the creating subject

sysmon-network.format: Windows Sysmon XML/EVTX, rendered as key=value by the forwarder
sysmon-network.subject: Image
sysmon-network.object: QueryName for DNS records, DestinationHostname otherwise
sysmon-network.join: ProcessGuid attributes the exchange to the process the process-profile recorded

suricata-http.subject: the server side of the flow, named by http.hostname when present, else dest_ip
suricata-http.join: flow_id groups a request with its response and with the flow record carrying the endpoints

nginx-access.subject: the serving host, from the server_name field or the log's own host tag
nginx-access.object: the path of the request line
nginx-access.class: request method GET/HEAD -> read; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE -> write
nginx-access.join: one line is one complete operation; no join needed

paloalto-traffic.format: PAN-OS TRAFFIC and THREAT syslog, comma-separated
paloalto-traffic.subject: the destination host, from dst
paloalto-traffic.object: misc, which carries the URI for THREAT url-filtering records
paloalto-traffic.class: THREAT url records -> read; TRAFFIC session records -> connect
paloalto-traffic.join: session id links a THREAT record to the TRAFFIC session that carried it

crushftp-session.selects: lines carrying a session identifier and a command verb
crushftp-session.subject: the service process recorded by the application, not the OS image
crushftp-session.object: the path or resource the command names
crushftp-session.peer: the client address the session opened with
crushftp-session.class: download/read verbs -> read; upload/zip/write verbs -> write
crushftp-session.join: the session identifier carries the client endpoint from the session-open line onto every later command line
